analyst_view.overall: This is a top-four clash. Twente have the league's best defence (10 conceded) and Ajax are the only Eredivisie side unbeaten away. Both won in the Conference League in midweek: Twente came from behind to beat Pafos 3-1 and Ajax won 6-1 at Midtjylland. Ajax coach Míchel says Caio Henrique and Oliver Edvardsen are available, Sofyan Amrabat is likely fit, Julian Brandt is possible and Anton Gaaei is 50-50, so Ajax should be stronger than the site's injury list suggests.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals. Both attacks are flying: Twente have 20 goals in their last six and Ajax 17, including the 6-1 in Denmark with two from Tolu Arokodare. Players returning for Ajax (Amrabat, Edvardsen, possibly Brandt) strengthen the visitors, and one preview predicts 2-2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.9 corners. Twente at home are expected to have more of the territory, but Ajax are strong away. Nothing in the news moves the corner count away from the model.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.1 cards, which looks low for a top-of-the-table 'kraker' where either side could end the weekend top. One report says the Twente camp, including coach John van den Brom, has publicly challenged Ajax to come to Enschede, which hints at a lively build-up. Joey Kooij referees.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.7 shots, with Twente expected to take most of them. Ajax getting players back should make the game more even than the model's 20-11 split, but the total already allows for a busy game, so we stay close to it.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target. With both teams scoring freely and Ajax's attack boosted by returning players, we expect a few more efforts on target than the model.
